sources.name: Kubernetes application logs
sources.description: Everything the services in the cluster logged, shipped through logstash (topic kube_apps, stakan cluster_a). The place to look for an error a user hit. Query the last 24 hours first and widen only when a trace leads earlier: this stream keeps about a week (the oldest documents were from the end of October), and a window before that returns nothing without saying why.

fieldHints.name: user_id
fieldHints.description: Client id of the person the request was made for, e.g. XC9DB5.

fieldHints.name: trace_id
fieldHints.description: One id for a whole request path across services; the fastest way from an error to its neighbours.

fieldHints.name: level
fieldHints.description: INFO, DEBUG, WARN or ERROR. ERROR carries the exception in stack_trace.

fieldHints.name: api_method
fieldHints.description: The API method that was called, e.g. getAdvertOffers.

fieldHints.name: app_id.keyword
fieldHints.description: Which service wrote the line, e.g. restrictions-api, enp-api, compliance-api.

fieldHints.name: phase
fieldHints.description: Where in the call path the line was written: thrift_in, thrift_out, thrift_err, browser -> nodejs, nodejs -> middle, middle -> nodejs.

fieldHints.name: kubernetes.pod_name
fieldHints.description: Pod instance, when the same service runs in several replicas.

fieldHints.name: duration_ms
fieldHints.description: How long the call took, in milliseconds.

fieldHints.name: container_version
fieldHints.description: Build of the service, useful to tell whether a bug came with a release.
